newDescription:
In this Year 3 Maths lesson, pupils learn how to multiply using the grid method by partitioning a two-digit number into tens and ones, multiplying each part, and then adding the partial products.

This lesson includes:
✔ Using known times-table facts to solve larger multiplications
✔ Splitting two-digit numbers into tens and ones
✔ Understanding partitioning as breaking a number into useful parts
✔ Using arrays and grouped representations to support multiplication
✔ Setting up a grid correctly for a two-digit by one-digit multiplication
✔ Multiplying the tens part and the ones part separately
✔ Using place value to scale known facts, such as using 2 × 4 to help calculate 20 × 4
✔ Adding partial products to find the final answer
✔ Explaining each stage of the grid method clearly
✔ Applying the method to increasingly challenging examples

Pupils begin by using familiar multiplication facts and partitioning numbers, for example splitting 15 into 10 and 5 or 17 into 10 and 7. This prepares them for the structure of the grid method.

The lesson then introduces the grid method explicitly. Pupils partition the larger number into tens and ones, place those parts across the top of the grid, write the one-digit multiplier down the side, calculate each product, and add the answers together.

Worked examples include 22 × 4, followed by independent practice with 13 × 4, 27 × 8 and 46 × 8.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to partition a two-digit number, set up a multiplication grid, calculate each partial product accurately, and combine the parts to solve two-digit by one-digit multiplication.
